title: The popular version. YouTube started as a dating site.
description:
YouTube started as a dating site. The source is co-founder Jawed Karim himself, in a 2007 commencement speech at the University of Illinois.

He said they called it that to generate interest. His words: "To generate interest we just said it was a new kind of dating site." The slogan was "Tune in, Hook up."

Karim said there was no good way to find video clips of it online. By February 2005 he and two PayPal colleagues were discussing a video sharing website.

What they offered women for every video uploaded, in Craigslist posts in Los Angeles and Las Vegas.

So Karim filled it with videos of 747s. By June the site was revamped to be more open and more general.

The dating line was the pitch. The idea was video.

Sources:
- https://commencement.illinois.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/JawedKarimCommencementAddress.pdf (read): Jawed Karim's own commencement address. Quotes: "To generate interest we just said it was a new kind of dating site"; the slogan "Tune in , Hook up"; they spammed Craigslist in Los Angeles and Las Vegas offering twenty dollars for every video uploaded; he filled the site with videos of 747s; "By June we had completely revamped the website, making it more open, and more general"; the December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami and no good way to find the clips; by February 2005 he and two PayPal colleagues were discussing a video sharing website.
- https://vice.com/en/article/10-years-ago-today-youtube-launched-as-a-dating-website (read): Vice, 23 April 2015, describes the dating origin as rumoured and passed off as fact in books, and relies on Karim's account; used only to confirm the speech is the source of the story and the twenty dollar figure.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_YouTube (read): founders Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim; site activated 14 February 2005.
